diagnostic_evidence.quote: We assume the existence of a constant~$\gamma$ in $(0,1)$ such that each element of~$\Tcalh$ is star-shaped with respect to a ball of radius larger than or equal to the diameter of that element;
moreover, we assume quasi-uniformity of the mesh, i.e.,

issues.failure_explanation: The standing mesh assumptions are impossible as stated. Quasi-uniformity is written as $\h_2\le\gamma\h_1$ with $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and $\h_1\le\h_2$; since $\gamma\h_1\le\gamma\h_2<\h_2$ for any element of positive diameter, no nondegenerate mesh satisfies it. Likewise, an element of diameter $h$ cannot be star-shaped with respect to a ball of radius $\ge h$ (such a ball has diameter $\ge 2h$ and, under the standard definition, must be contained in the element). The intended standard conditions (star-shapedness with respect to a ball of radius $\ge\gamma$ times the diameter; $\h_2\le C\h_1$ with $C\ge1$) are not what is written, and the quasi-uniformity clause admits several non-equivalent repairs.

failure_location.quote: given~$\h_1$ and~$\h_2$ the diameters of two arbitrary elements with $\h_1\le \h_2$, one has $\h_2 \le \gamma \h_1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the assumptions in standard form: each element star-shaped with respect to a ball of radius $\ge\gamma$ times its diameter ($\gamma\in(0,1)$), and quasi-uniformity $\h_2\le C\h_1$ for arbitrary element diameters with an explicit constant $C\ge1$.
issues.overall_effect: As literally stated, the hypotheses on the spatial mesh (used e.g. for the elliptic-projection bounds \eqref{elliptic-projector} and \eqref{elliptic-projector-L2-stab}, cf. the attached footnote) admit no instance, so the stated scope of the whole framework is empty as written.
issues.title: Contradictory mesh shape-regularity and quasi-uniformity assumptions
issues.why_classification: Local corrections with standard constants restore the intended hypotheses; no inference, rate, or guarantee is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality \eqref{inequality-step-n} is per-interval and its left-hand side contains only the single jump term $\frac14\|\jump{\uh'}(t_{n-1})\|^2$. Using it at $n=m$ together with the iterated estimate from testing with $\uh'$ (third quote, in which the jumps have been dropped) bounds only $\frac14\|\jump{\uh'}(t_{m-1})\|^2$. The claimed intermediate display instead contains $\frac14\sum_{n=1}^m\|\jump{\uh'}(t_{n-1})\|^2$, which follows from neither route: summing \eqref{inequality-step-n} over $n\le m$ leaves the uncontrolled sum of grid energies $\sum_{n\le m}E_{n-1}$, and bounding each $E_{n-1}$ via the iterated estimate costs an extra factor up to $m$ (or exponential in $N$ via the recursion) in the forcing term, contradicting the constant-free claim. A necessary step controlling the jump sum is missing.

failure_location.quote: in~\eqref{inequality-step-n}, selecting~$n$ to be~$m=m(\uh)$ as in~\eqref{selecting-m}, and combining the two displays give

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Control the jump sum by summing the un-iterated per-step energy identity obtained by testing with $\uh'$ (the mechanism cited as \cite[eq. (4.1)]{Walkington:2014} and invoked again in Remark \ref{remark:jumps-in-error}), which gives $E_m+\frac12\sum_{n\le m}\|\jump{\uh'}(t_{n-1})\|^2\le E_0+(\sum_n\|\Pizpbftmo f\|_{L^1(I_n)})(\ldots)^{1/2}$, and combine it with \eqref{inequality-step-n} at $n=m$; the theorem survives with slightly adjusted numerical constants.
issues.overall_effect: The jump-sum term in the stability estimate \eqref{discrete-stability-estimate} is unproven as written, and the jump-sum term in the conclusion of Lemma \ref{lemma:estimates-xih} inherits the gap. The $L^\infty$-type part of the stability estimate, on which Theorems \ref{theorem:abstract-convergence} and \ref{theorem:h-p-convergence} rely, is unaffected.
issues.title: Stability proof does not derive the sum of derivative jumps
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a short, standard summation of an identity already cited in the paper; the theorem's structure, scaling, and constant-free character are preserved, with only the explicit numerical constants changing.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \overset{\eqref{equivalent-definition-Pcalpt}}{=} - ( (u-\Pcalpbftt u)'(\tnmo,\cdot), q_{\pnt-1}(\tnmo,\cdot))_{\mathcal X} \overset{\eqref{equivalent-definition-Pcalpt}}{=} (\jump{(\Pcalpbftt u)'}(\tnmo,\cdot), q_{\pnt-1}(\tnmo,\cdot))_{\mathcal X},

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side involves $\jump{(\Pcalpbftt u)'}(t_{n-1})$, a difference of one-sided derivatives that requires $\Pcalpbftt u$ (hence $u$) on the previous slab and, at $n=1$, a convention for the value at $0^-$; the hypothesis $u\in H^2(I_n;\mathcal X)$ provides neither, so the statement is ill-defined at $n=1$. Moreover, the proof's second invocation of \eqref{equivalent-definition-Pcalpt} equates $-(u-\Pcalpbftt u)'(t_{n-1}^+)$ with the jump, which is valid only if $u'(t_{n-1}^+)=u'(t_{n-1}^-)$, i.e. under continuity of $u'$ across $t_{n-1}$ — a hypothesis that is not stated and is needed without being established.

failure_location.quote: For all~$u$ in $H^2(\In;\mathcal X)$ and all~$q_{\pnt-1}$ in~$\Pbb_{\pnt-1}(\In;\mathcal X)$, the following identity holds true:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the lemma for functions $u$ that are piecewise $H^2$ on the time grid with $u$ and $u'$ continuous across $t_{n-1}$ (e.g. $u\in H^2(0,T;\mathcal X)$), together with the convention $(\Pcalpbftt u)'(0^-):=u'(0)$.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's statement is not well posed as written. Its only application (in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma:estimates-xih}) concerns the exact solution, which is smooth in time, so no downstream result is lost once the hypotheses are repaired.
issues.title: Lemma hypothesis does not define the interface jump (missing continuity of $u'$ and $t_0$ convention)
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis and an explicit $t_0$ convention make the statement well defined and the proof valid with no loss; the application satisfies the added hypotheses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The properties of the $L^2$ and $H^1$ projectors imply $\Pizpbftmo w' = (\Pionepbft w)'$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition and its proof use the $H^1$ projector $\Pionepbft$ onto degree-$\pnt$ polynomials clamped at $\tnmo$, which is never defined: \eqref{Pionetpmo} defines $\Pionepbftmo$, projecting onto $\Pbb_{\pnt-1}$. For the defined operator the key identity $\Pizpbftmo w'=(\Pionepbftmo w)'$ is false (the left side has degree $\pnt$, the right side degree $\pnt-1$; in fact $(\Pionepbftmo w)'=\Pizpbftmth w'$), and the endpoint condition recalled from \eqref{Pionetpmo} is also attributed to the wrong operator. The decomposition $T_1=(w-\Pionepbft w)$ central to the proof rests on an object undefined in the source. (The proof of \eqref{Pcaltildept-L2-approx-bis} also cites \eqref{Pcaltildept-L2-approx-bis} itself instead of \eqref{Pcaltildept-L2-approx}.)

failure_location.quote: Let~$\Pcalpbftt$ and~$\Pionepbftmo$ be the operators in~\eqref{equivalent-definition-Pcalpt} and~\eqref{Pionetpmo}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\Pionepbft$ (the $H^1$ projection onto $\Pbb_{\pnt}(\In;\mathcal X)$ with $(w-\Pionepbft w)(\tnmo,\cdot)=0$) in \eqref{Pionetpmo} or separately, and use it consistently in the statement and proof; then $\Pizpbftmo w'=(\Pionepbft w)'$ and the argument goes through unchanged, and fix the self-citation.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's proof is invalid as written. Downstream uses (the bounds on $\gimel_5$ and $\gimel_8$ in Theorem \ref{theorem:h-p-convergence}) rely only on the approximation conclusion, which is correct for the degree-$\pnt$ clamped $H^1$ projector, so they are restored by the local repair.
issues.title: Approximation proposition invokes an undefined projector; the defined one falsifies the proof's identity
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local, essentially forced operator definition; the stated bounds are exactly what the corrected proof yields, so no claim or downstream result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In words, $\xih$ is the solution to method~\eqref{Walkington:method} with right-hand side given by $(\fxih,\vtau)_{L^2(0,T;L^2(\Omega))}$ with

issues.failure_explanation: Deriving the $\xih$ equation with right-hand side \eqref{fxih} requires Lemma \ref{lem:added-1} at $n=1$, which forces the convention $(\Pcalpbftt\PihEcal u)'(0^-)=\PihEcal u'(0)=\PihEcal\uone$. With that equation, the weakly imposed initial derivative produced by the stability estimate is $(\xih^-)'(0)=\PihEcal\uone-\uoneh$, so the initial term is $\frac12\|\PihEcal\uone-\uoneh\|^2$. The proof instead evaluates $(\xih^-)'(0)=\uoneh-(\Pcalpbftt\PihEcal u)'(0)$, the right derivative at $0$; this value is compatible only with a different representation of the same equation whose right-hand side on $I_1$ differs from \eqref{fxih} by $(\Pcalpbftt\PihEcal u)''-(\PihEcal u)''$, whose pairings with the test space equal $((\Pcalpbftt\PihEcal u)'(0^+)-\PihEcal\uone, q(0))$ and are nonzero in general. The two representations are mixed, so the bound of $T_{1,2}$ — hence the lemma's terms $\|\uone-(\Pcalpbftt u)'(0)\|^2$ and $\|(\Pcalpbftt(I-\PihEcal)u)'(0)\|^2$ — is unjustified. The correct term $\|\PihEcal\uone-\uoneh\|^2$ requires an additional $\|(I-\PihEcal)\uone\|$-type contribution absent from the stated bound; for elliptic-regularity exponent $\alpha<1$ this contribution is of lower order than the stated $\|\uone-\uoneh\|^2$, so the lemma as stated can fail.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the $t=0$ bookkeeping: use $(\xih^-)'(0)=\PihEcal\uone-\uoneh$ with the \eqref{fxih} right-hand side, bound it by $\|(I-\PihEcal)\uone\|^2+\|\uone-\uoneh\|^2$, and remove the $\gimel_3$ term and the $\tauo$-dependent part of $\gimel_4$ from the theorems (the needed $\|(I-\PihEcal)\uone\|$-bound is already the second part of \eqref{estimate-gimel4}); all rates of the corollary are then recovered.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bounds of Lemma \ref{lemma:estimates-xih}, Theorem \ref{theorem:abstract-convergence} and Theorem \ref{theorem:h-p-convergence} (the $\gimel_3$ term and the first part of $\gimel_4$) are not established and the lemma's statement is incorrect in general; Corollary \ref{corollary:h-p-convergence-alpha=1} is derived through this chain. The final convergence rates survive the repair.
issues.title: Misidentified initial-derivative term in the estimate for $\xih$
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and preserves all convergence rates, but it is a nontrivial rederivation that changes the explicit statements of one lemma and two theorems, and the uncorrected lemma is false in parameter regimes ($\alpha<1$) that the paper's assumptions allow.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, we focus on the first term on the right-hand side: for any~$\qpx$ in $W^{1,\infty}(\Ik; \Vh)$,

issues.failure_explanation: The quoted sub-term of the $\gimel_7$ bound controls the purely spatial error $\|(u-\PihEcal u)'\|^2_{L^\infty(\Ik;L^2)}$, which the proof bounds by spatial polynomial approximation of degree $\px$ (test functions $\qpx\in W^{1,\infty}(\Ik;\Vh)$ and the elliptic projector). Yet both the proof display and the theorem's statement write the time degree $\pkt$ and its powers in this term. As stated the bound is false: under $p$-refinement in time at fixed spatial mesh and fixed $\px$, the displayed term tends to zero like $(\pkt)^{-2s-2}$ while the spatial error it must bound does not decrease. The proof's own combination step, which factors $(1+\h^{-2+2\alpha}/\px^{-2+2\alpha})$, shows that $\px$ is the intended degree.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\pkt$ (and its powers) by $\px$ in the two spatial-approximation sub-terms of the $\gimel_7$ part of the theorem's display and in the corresponding proof displays.
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicit displayed form of the a priori bound in Theorem \ref{theorem:h-p-convergence} is affected (the two spatial-approximation sub-terms of the $\gimel_7$ part); the proof establishes the corrected bound, and in Corollary \ref{corollary:h-p-convergence-alpha=1} one has $\px=\pnt=\p$, so no downstream rate is affected.
issues.title: Time degree written in place of spatial degree in the a priori bound
issues.why_classification: The correction is single and forced (the terms are spatial errors and the proof's own algebra uses $\px$), local to a few displays, and preserves all claims and rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Due to~\eqref{consequence:convexity}, for all $n=1,\dots,N$, we have the following identity in $L^2(\Omega)$ inside each time interval:

issues.failure_explanation: The reliability analysis and the estimator require $H^2$-type spatial regularity of $\utau$, although the trial space $\Xtau$ is only $H^1_0$-valued. The implication '$\Deltax u\in L^2(0,T;L^2)$ implies $\Deltax \utau\in L^2(0,T;L^2)$' in \eqref{consequence:convexity} is asserted without proof and is nontrivial (it needs a mode-wise regularity-transfer argument for the DG-CG scheme in $\Deltax$-weighted norms; the tacit commutation $\Deltax(\Rcalppoutau)=\Rcalppo(\Deltax\utau)$ used when applying \eqref{Wihler-3} and \eqref{eq: L2 orthogonality} to $\Deltax$-quantities is likewise never established). Moreover, the estimator and the bound contain $\|\jump{\Deltax\utau'}(\tnmo)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$; at $n=1$ this equals $\Deltax\utau'(0^+)-\Deltax\uone$, which is not even defined unless $\Deltax\uone\in L^2(\Omega)$ (i.e. $\uone$ of $H^2$ type), whereas \eqref{assumption:convexity} assumes only $\uone\in H^1_0(\Omega)$; mode-wise, stiff-mode contributions to such $\Deltax$-weighted jumps scale with $\|\Deltax\uone\|$, so their finiteness under the stated data is unestablished. The identity \eqref{discrete-star-identity} 'in $L^2(\Omega)$' and the estimator's well-definedness rest on these unproven premises.

failure_location.quote: Let assumption~\eqref{assumption:convexity} hold true, which implies~\eqref{consequence:convexity}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the data assumptions (e.g. $\uone\in H^2(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, so that $\Deltax\uone\in L^2(\Omega)$) and prove the regularity transfer $\Deltax\utau\in L^2(0,T;L^2(\Omega))$ together with the $\Deltax$-commutation of the reconstruction via a contained mode-wise argument; or restate \eqref{consequence:convexity} as a joint assumption on both $u$ and $\utau$, withdrawing the claim that \eqref{assumption:convexity} is sufficient.
issues.overall_effect: Propositions \ref{proposition:initial-reliability-estimate} and \ref{proposition:reliability-estimate} (the paper's second main contribution) are at best conditionally valid: under the stated sufficient conditions \eqref{assumption:convexity} the estimator may be undefined or infinite and the derivation of \eqref{discrete-star-identity} is unjustified.
issues.title: A posteriori framework rests on unproven spatial regularity of the semi-discrete solution
issues.why_classification: A supported resolution avoiding new global proof architecture exists (stronger data assumptions plus a contained but genuinely nontrivial regularity proof, or an explicit joint assumption) and the reliability bounds survive recognizably intact; however, part of the advertised regime ($\uone\in H^1_0(\Omega)$) is excluded and a new argument is required.
